test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Machinist) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following options correctly describes the axis convention in a CNC turning centre?

options.text: The spindle axis is designated as Y and the radial axis toward the tool post is X.
The spindle axis is designated as Z and the radial axis away from the tool post is Y.
The spindle axis is designated as X and the radial axis toward the tool post is Z.
The spindle axis is designated as Z and the radial axis toward the tool post is X.

solution:
The correct answer is __The spindle axis is designated as Z and the radial axis toward the tool post is X**(Option 4)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• CNC Turning Centre Axis Convention:__ The spindle axis is always designated as the Z-axis.
 
• The radial axis, which is perpendicular to the spindle axis, is designated as the X-axis.
 
• The tool movement toward or away from the workpiece along the radial direction is controlled by the X-axis.
 
• The Z-axis corresponds to the tool's movement along the spindle axis (longitudinal direction).
 
• This convention is standardized for CNC turning centers to maintain uniformity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Machine Tool Axis Systems:**

 
 
• CNC machines use a Cartesian coordinate system to define tool movement.
 
• For turning centers, the Z-axis aligns with the spindle, while the X-axis is perpendicular to it.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Axis Convention:**
 
 
• Consistency ensures easier programming and operation across machines.
 
• Understanding axis conventions is essential for accurate machining and setup.
